en: The Apadāna of the Elder Uddālakapupphiya Mandāravapupphiya Chapter 7, Number 7 I offered a single uddālaka flower at the feet of the Buddha Vipassī, who was seated upon his seat of enlightenment. Because of that root of merit, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand world-ages. Having passed through those births, I have now reached this final existence. Having abandoned all defilements, I have attained parinibbāna. My mind is liberated from the five lower fetters. This is my final body; there will be no further birth. This is the account of the Elder Uddālakapupphiya.
“At that time, a perfectly enlightened Buddha named Anoma was dwelling on the bank of the Ganges;
having taken hold of an uddālaka flower, [he offered it].”
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
because I offered that flower, [I attained this fruit].
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Uddālakapupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Uddālakapupphiya is the seventh.
